clue.text: Island valley with one of its lakes very big

indicators.note: the valley word has two letters standing for lakes, and one of them gives way to the next piece

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A traveller describes an island whose valley holds one enormous lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with one of its lakes very big' swaps one L of DELL (L = lake) for OS, leaving DEL + OS.
explanation.definitionFit: Delos is a small Greek island in the Cyclades, the mythical birthplace of Apollo and Artemis.

clue.text: Threats to tanks? Then road gets tricky

indicators.note: tricky marks the letters as twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A road becomes difficult to drive along, a danger to armoured vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges THEN ROAD GETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragon's teeth are rows of concrete pyramids built as anti-tank obstacles in the Second World War.

clue.text: Machine offers French word and English translation

parts.note: la is a French word for 'the'
the English rendering of French la is the

explanation.surface: A device comes with a French label and its English version.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece translates the first: French LA is English THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine tool that turns wood or metal against a cutter.

clue.text: Voyager landing on planet — hard or squishy territory?

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece lands on top of the next, coming before it

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor, a voyager
Mars is a planet
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A space probe touches down on a planet whose ground may be firm or soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voyager' suggests the space probe; it is SALT, a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt marsh is coastal land flooded by the tide, soggy ground.

clue.text: Opposition of French fellow coming up for match?

parts.note: de is the French word for 'of'
a fiancé is a man engaged and so heading towards a marriage, a match

explanation.surface: A Frenchman rising to take on a sporting fixture meets resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' tempts you to write F; it is part of the longer phrase for an engaged man, the 'match' being a marriage, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is open resistance to authority, a form of opposition.

clue.text: They may be on hand to help the barely numerate

definitions.text: They may be on hand to help the barely numerate

parts.words: They may be on hand to help the barely numerate
parts.note: fingers are on a hand, and someone poor at sums counts on them; the word also means numerals

explanation.definitionFit: Fingers are found on the hand, and numerals are used by those counting; both senses share one word.

clue.text: What it is difficult to hide after a recession?

definitions.text: What it is difficult to hide after a recession?

parts.words: What it is difficult to hide after a recession?
parts.note: the recession is a receding hairline, which leaves the top of the face exposed and hard to cover

explanation.definitionFit: A receding hairline exposes more brow, the part of the face above the eyes.

clue.text: Minister lacking power as female parliamentarian

indicators.note: lacking means the clergyman's word goes without the letter for power

parts.note: a pastor is a minister of religion
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A clergyman without influence is compared to a woman MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests government; it is a clergyman. Nancy Astor was the first woman to take her seat in the British House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Astor became the first woman to sit as an MP in 1919.

clue.text: Word in scr about university fellowship

indicators.note: about means going around, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: SCR stands for Senior Common Room in British colleges, so a word in it is common

explanation.surface: In the senior common room a word circulates about a university's fellowship.
explanation.walkthrough: SCR, the Senior Common Room, is the staff lounge in Oxford and Cambridge colleges; its middle word is COMMON.
explanation.definitionFit: Communion is a sharing of thoughts or fellowship between people.

clue.text: Tailoring maths specially for numbers of mathematicians

indicators.note: the letters are specially rearranged, made up to order like a tailored suit

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher adapts the maths syllabus specially for students of mathematics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailoring' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'specially' rearranges TAILORING MATHS.
explanation.definitionFit: An antilogarithm is the number whose logarithm is a given value, the kind of figure found in a mathematician's tables.

clue.text: Farm worker taking coat off

parts.note: the coat taken off is the fleece of an animal, not the worker's own jacket

explanation.definitionFit: A shearer clips the woolly fleece from flock animals.

clue.text: Outshine dull companion when going after maiden?

parts.note: in cricket, a maiden over is an over with no runs scored, so the word following 'maiden' is over
matt, also spelt mat, means dull or without shine
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A drab partner is chasing a young woman, hoping to outshine rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over is a cricket over in which the bowler concedes no runs. CH, Companion of Honour, is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To overmatch is to be more than a match for someone, to surpass them.

clue.text: Rasping sound of bird

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word that is pronounced like the bird's name when spoken

parts.note: the ruff is a wading bird of the sandpiper family

explanation.surface: A bird gives out a harsh, grating call.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasping voice is harsh and grating, as a rough one is.

clue.text: Once bore son to such a theatrical fellow

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
Brendan Behan's play is The Quare Fellow, so its fellow is described as quare, Irish for odd

explanation.surface: A theatrical man was once told he had produced a son.
explanation.walkthrough: The Quare Fellow is a 1954 play by the Irish writer Brendan Behan; quare is Irish English for strange. 'Once' marks the dated slang sense of a dull conventional person.
explanation.definitionFit: Square was 1950s-60s slang for a dull, conventional person, a tedious type out of step with fashion.

clue.text: Get rid of loveless marriages? Improbable

indicators.note: loveless removes the letter shaped like a zero, love in tennis scoring

parts.note: unions are marriages
a tall story is an improbable one

explanation.surface: Marriages without love are unlikely to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops the O (love = zero) from UNIONS, leaving UNINS; TALL as in a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: To uninstall software is to remove it from a computer.

clue.text: Medical institution to get endless money? That's optimistic!

parts.note: a san is short for sanatorium, a medical institution

indicators.note: the coin's name loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: a guinea is an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a hospital will receive an unending supply of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last A from GUINEA, an old British coin worth one pound and one shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine means cheerfully confident about the future.

clue.text: River bird about to fill its stomach?

indicators.note: about here means around, so the bird holds the eating word

parts.note: a grouse is a game bird
to eat is to fill the stomach

explanation.surface: A river bird is about to have a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Ouse is a river in eastern England, flowing through Bedford and Ely to the Wash.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Ouse is a long English river flowing to the Wash.

clue.text: A bit of plumbing can be installed on island if really necessary

indicators.note: in a down answer the fitting placed on top comes before the island

parts.note: a tap is part of a plumbing system
inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: Some plumbing can be fitted on an island if absolutely required.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH is Scots for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pinch means in an emergency, when needed.

clue.text: Plant they sprinkled after return of hose?

indicators.note: after says the scrambled pronoun comes behind the turned-round piece
return means the word for a hose is taken back the other way

parts.note: a hose is a flexible pipe

indicators.note: sprinkled scatters the letters of the word they into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gardeners watered a plant once the hose had come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hose' suggests stockings but is a garden hose, and 'Plant' is a living one that grows perched on trees; 'return of' turns the tube round, and 'sprinkled' scrambles the pronoun, placed 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphyte is a plant growing on another plant without feeding on it, as many orchids and mosses do.

clue.text: Economist giving set of answers to head shortly

parts.note: a key is the list of solutions to a test or puzzle

indicators.note: shortly means the headland word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: An economist hands a crib sheet to a principal in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims NESS (a headland) to NES. 'head' looks like a boss, but it is a promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the British economist behind Keynesian theory.

clue.text: In birthday suit a French boy catches cold

indicators.note: catches means the pair of words hold the next letter between them

parts.note: un is French for a
a lad is a boy
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A naked French boy catches a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' suggests catching a chill, as the naked boy might; here it means holding the abbreviation for cold inside the French-plus-boy pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in one's birthday suit means naked, unclothed.

clue.text: Stunner posed again, but facing the wrong way

indicators.note: the retaken exam word is turned around and read in the opposite direction

parts.note: resat means sat again, as for a portrait or an exam

explanation.surface: A model posed a second time but faced away from the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing the wrong way' turns RESAT around. 'Stunner' suggests a beauty, but it is a stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric weapon that stuns its target.

clue.text: Artist and lecturer gas

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: A painter and a teacher chatter away.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas.

clue.text: Remorse of writer in church admitting heartless article

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so another piece goes inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A writer in church feels remorse for including a cruel piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the middle letter from the article to leave TE, which 'admitting' slots inside the preposition and church abbreviation, all after the writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitence is sorrow for having done wrong, regret.

clue.text: Prize giver presents book in festive season

indicators.note: in places the book letter inside the word for the festive season

parts.note: Noel is Christmas

explanation.surface: Someone hands out presents with a book at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' looks like gifts; it is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel founded the Nobel prizes through his will.

clue.text: It could be one songbird with a musical item

parts.note: the cardinal is a red North American songbird
a number is a song or piece in a show

explanation.surface: A singing bird joins a song in a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the definition by example: one is a counting number.
explanation.definitionFit: A counting number such as one, two or three is the kind used for quantity rather than order.

clue.text: Faded rebel, dull in external appearance

indicators.note: the dull word appears on the outside with the rebel sitting inside it

parts.note: bland means dull or insipid
Che Guevara is the famous revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel has faded, looking dull from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Che (Guevara) the revolutionary goes inside BLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanched means whitened or drained of colour, pale.

clue.text: Always engaging extremely useful mathematician

indicators.note: engaging means taking something in, so the poetic word for always holds the next piece

parts.note: e'er is the poetic short form of ever, meaning always

indicators.note: extremely picks out the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A very useful mathematician is always engaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives UL, the first and last letters of 'useful'; E'ER is poetic for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was the eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician famous for e and graph theory.
